title: Buckaroo Bowl I
dek: The first championship game in Buckaroo Football League history, a two-week total in NFL weeks 17 and 18 of 2023, in which top-seeded Habibsters (Kaushal) erased a 19.8-point deficit and beat Team Pillbert (Alan) 251.36 to 192.08.
body: Buckaroo Bowl I was the championship game of the Buckaroo Football League's inaugural 2023 season, played as a two-week total across NFL weeks 17 and 18. It matched the league's top two seeds: Habibsters, managed by Kaushal, and Team Pillbert, managed by Alan. Because it was the first title game the league ever staged, neither manager entered with a championship to his name, and the winner was guaranteed a permanent place as the league's first champion.

Habibsters earned the No. 1 seed with a 10-4 regular-season record and a league-leading total of 1,528.8 points. Team Pillbert finished one game back at 9-5 as the No. 2 seed, with 1,499.3 points, a gap of 29.5 points over fourteen weeks. Going in, Luffy rated the game close to a coin flip, giving Habibsters a 52 percent title chance and Team Pillbert 48 percent.

The two teams split their regular-season meetings. Team Pillbert won the first in week 5 by a lopsided 116.72 to 75.76, while Habibsters took the rematch in week 10 by just 3.04 points, 109.48 to 106.44. With one blowout and one nail-biter on the ledger, the series offered little guidance beyond the fact that Philly had the bigger single win and Habib had the more recent one.

Each team reached the Bowl through a single two-week semifinal played in NFL weeks 15 and 16. Habibsters faced Dawgs (Mekhi) and won 237.54 to 196.12, a 41.42-point margin. The semifinal was carried by Christian McCaffrey, who posted 61.3 points over the two weeks, the top individual total of the round for Habibsters.

Team Pillbert met The fumblers (Randy) in the other semifinal and advanced 234.86 to 216.44, an 18.42-point margin. Jalen Hurts led the way with 45.4 points. Both finalists cleared 230 points in their semifinals, setting up a title game between the two highest-seeded and, by regular-season points, two most productive teams in the league.

Week 17 belonged to Team Pillbert, which led 131.4 to 111.6 after the first half of the two-week total. Habibsters opened the scoring early in the week, when Dak Prescott hit CeeDee Lamb for a 92-yard touchdown in the first quarter of Detroit at Dallas. Prescott added an 8-yard touchdown pass to Brandin Cooks in the fourth quarter, and Amon-Ra St. Brown answered for the Lions in the same game with an 11-yard touchdown catch from Jared Goff, giving Kaushal production on both sidelines. The Bills D/ST chipped in a defensive score when Rasul Douglas returned an interception 40 yards for a touchdown in the second quarter against New England.

Team Pillbert's week 17 surge came from a cluster of multi-touchdown efforts. In the Rams' game at the Giants, Kyren Williams ran for scores of 4, 2 and 28 yards, and Cooper Kupp caught a 5-yard touchdown from Matthew Stafford. Jalen Hurts threw three touchdown passes against Arizona, two to Julio Jones from 12 and 22 yards and a 9-yarder to Dallas Goedert. Deebo Samuel caught a 2-yard touchdown against Washington, a game in which Habibsters kicker Jake Moody made field goals of 38 and 22 yards, and Joe Mixon caught a 7-yard touchdown from Jake Browning at Kansas City after Evan McPherson opened that game with a 34-yard field goal.

Team Pillbert started week 18 strongly as well. Mixon scored twice in the first quarter against Cleveland, on a 1-yard run and a 6-yard catch, and McPherson added a 45-yard field goal in the second. Those were nearly the last points Alan's side would collect from that game onward: Tyreek Hill's 3-yard touchdown catch against Buffalo in the second quarter was the only other Team Pillbert touchdown of the week. Williams, Kupp and David Njoku recorded zero points in week 18, and Hurts managed 0.6.

Habibsters, meanwhile, scored from all over the board. Tony Pollard ran in a 1-yard touchdown for Dallas at Washington. In Jacksonville's game at Tennessee, Calvin Ridley caught a 59-yard touchdown from Trevor Lawrence in the second quarter and Evan Engram added a 14-yard score in the fourth. Josh Allen threw touchdown passes to Trent Sherfield and Dawson Knox in Miami, and in the fourth quarter of Minnesota at Detroit, St. Brown put an exclamation point on the title with a 70-yard touchdown from Goff. Habibsters won week 18 by 139.8 to 60.7, a 79.1-point swing that turned a 19.8-point deficit into a 59.3-point championship margin, 251.36 to 192.08.

Amon-Ra St. Brown was the standout of the game for Habibsters, scoring 43 points against a projection of 29.7, well above his season average of 14.3 points per start; his 70-yard week 18 touchdown was the longest play by either team's starters in the second week. The quarterback pairing of Dak Prescott (45.5 points, projected 43.2) and Josh Allen (44.2 points, projected 39.9, against a season average of 23.2) gave Kaushal nearly 90 points from the position. Evan Engram added 27.9 against a 19.2 projection, roughly triple his 9.2-point season average, and the two defenses Habib used delivered big: the Bills D/ST scored 19 in week 17 and the Jets D/ST 18 in week 18, each against projections of about 8.

Not everything went to plan for the champions. Rachaad White finished with 17.9 points against a projection of 30, Austin Ekeler with 11.9 against 26.6, and Christian McCaffrey, the semifinal hero, with 11.1 against 23.2, all of it in week 17. Kicker Jake Moody totaled 10 against a 16.7 projection. Habibsters also left 46 points on the bench in Najee Harris, more than any player Kaushal started, though the margin made it a footnote rather than a regret.

For Team Pillbert, Joe Mixon was the best performer with 40.9 points against a 29.3 projection, more than triple his 12.8-point season average, and Kyren Williams scored 29.1 against a projection of 19, all in week 17. The most costly shortfall came at quarterback, where Jalen Hurts scored 19.8 points against a 44.2 projection, well below his 22.5-point season average, after just 0.6 in week 18. Tyreek Hill managed 28.3 against a 37.7 projection.

Alan's bench held 33.5 points from C.J. Stroud, 13.7 more than Hurts, plus 26 from Isiah Pacheco and 23.3 from Sam LaPorta. Even the most favorable lineup swaps, however, would have recovered less than 40 points, short of the 59.3-point final margin; Philly's lineup decisions shaped the score but did not decide the title.

The victory made Kaushal the first champion in Buckaroo Football League history and completed a season in which Habibsters led the league in regular-season points and held the top seed from start to finish of the playoffs. Habibsters finished first of six teams and Team Pillbert second. The 59.3-point margin made the inaugural Bowl a decisive one, despite Luffy's near-even pregame odds and a week 17 that had tilted firmly toward Team Pillbert.

For Alan, the game was a case of a strong first week undone by a collapse in the second, when his team scored just 60.7 points. Team Pillbert's runner-up finish nonetheless established it as one of the league's two best teams in its first season.

Habib's championship proved to be the start of a dynasty: Habibsters went on to win Buckaroo Bowl II in 2024 as well, making Kaushal the only manager to win the league's first two titles. At the other end of the 2023 standings, Ben Dover (Sonny) finished last through the consolation ladder, beginning a stretch at the bottom that would eventually give way to Sonny's own title run in Buckaroo Bowl III.
